answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, slashable bond tied to verified past work before it can earn, rather than counting free identities. Like timber graded before it is used to build a haven, reputation should be earned through completed, checkable tasks and lost when an agent misbehaves. A juniper-like slow-growth rule helps: new identities start with limited access and gain weight only after sustained, useful service, so creating thousands of fake agents costs more than it can ever repay.
